mindset: # V19 Gate 0 — ARCHITECTURE chain, lightweight end-to-end validation (NOT a scientific study)

This is an infrastructure Gate. The ONLY objective is to complete the full production loop — proposal, implementation, validation, real trial training, the forced formal path, inference, scoring, HealthGate evaluation, persistence, and the next iteration — under a deliberately reduced budget (trial 5 min, formal 30 min, tiny data portions).

Scientific competitiveness is explicitly NOT an objective of this Gate. Beating FCNet, beating V18, or maximizing denoising performance are all out of scope. A modest score with a correctly recorded outcome is a Gate success; an ambitious model that cannot finish is a Gate failure.
propose: Propose a compact, low-risk ARCHITECTURE change whose purpose is to complete the full training, inference, scoring, HealthGate, persistence, and next-iteration workflow under the reduced Gate budget. The architecture chain must still propose an architecture change, not merely a loss-only change.

Prefer small parameter counts (roughly 0.1-2 M parameters), conventional PyTorch operations (Conv1d, small dilated stacks, GRU, LayerNorm/GroupNorm, embedding + softmax heads), stable output distributions, simple tensor shapes, and fast execution.

Avoid FCNet-scale capacity, large attention stacks, expensive multi-stage models, unusually large hidden dimensions, quadratic full-sequence attention, or components that require long training to become numerically stable.

Everything must work at max_epochs=1 with ~2% training portions and finish a trial attempt well inside a 5-minute wall budget and a formal attempt well inside 30 minutes. Plan step counts and batch sizes for these budgets explicitly.
Keep the loss conservative: prefer a registered built-in loss (Branch A). Only use a custom loss if strictly necessary for output-contract compatibility.
implement: Implement through the existing model plugin contract with the simplest correct realization. Prioritize reliable implementation and numerical stability over any cleverness.
Keep tensor shapes simple and vectorized; no per-timestep Python loops in forward(). Keep the declared output contract ([B, T] int -> [B, 256, T] float) exactly.
If the proposal risks the Gate time budget, reduce step count or segment workload — for THIS Gate, small and finished beats large and killed.
tune: Tune minimally: conservative learning rates, batch sizes that fit comfortably, no aggressive exploration. The Gate has max_rounds=2 (one trial + the forced formal path) — plan for completion, not for score.
Respect the reduced budgets: trial 5 minutes, formal 30 minutes, portions ~2%/1% — never plan workloads sized for the production 20/120-minute budgets.
A HealthGate-invalid round is acceptable Gate output if recorded correctly; do not chase validity with risky changes inside this Gate.
validate: Validate strictly against the plugin contract; reject unimplementable or contract-violating code as usual. Gate speed is never a reason to weaken validation.
